C0.quote: the pairwise majority relation of this society is acyclic
C0.note: Borderline: the paper studies Condorcet domains (preference restrictions guaranteeing acyclic majority relation) combinatorially. Treated as ELIG since the domains concern properties of majority voting.

C1.quote: for any K the domain FK is a maximal Condorcet domain
C1.note: Structural and combinatorial characterisation of domains; maximality, connectedness, single-peakedness on a circle.

C2.1.value: linear orders (domain of linear orders; preferences)
C2.1.quote: A Condorcet domain is a set of linear orders on a given set of alternatives

C2.2.quote: By L(A) we will denote all linear orders on the set of alternatives A

C2.3.quote: all voters of a certain society are known to have preferences over those alternatives
C2.3.note: Voters are said to have preferences represented by linear orders.

C2.4.quote: have preferences over those alternatives represented by linear orders from that set
C2.4.note: Linear orders are described as voters' preferences and the majority relation is applied to them directly, with no statement about submission or reporting.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions for voters.

C5.1.note: Results are about domain structure, not welfare criteria.

VOT.note: Voters are not agents who act in the formal model.

claims.quote: they represent a compromise which allows a society to always have transitive collective decisions

C9.1.note: Motivational claim about maximal Condorcet domains in the introduction, about individual freedom for voters and societal collective decisions. Weak claim, but it concerns institutions and voters.

C9.2.quote: provide voters with as much individual freedom as possible
C9.2.note: Needs an assumption that voters' held preferences are submitted as the orders in the domain. The relation between submitted inputs and held preferences is not stated.
